verses.text: Then the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness so the devil could tempt him.
After fasting for forty days and forty nights, he was hungry.
The tempter came to him and said, “If you’re God’s Son, tell these stones to become bread.”
Jesus answered, “Scripture says, ‘A person doesn’t live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from God.’”
Then the devil took him to the holy city and set him on the highest point of the temple.
“If you’re God’s Son, jump down,” he said. “Scripture says, ‘He will command his angels to protect you,’ and, ‘They will catch you in their hands so you don’t even strike your foot against a stone.’”
Jesus told him, “Scripture also says, ‘Don’t put the Lord your God to the test.’”
Again, the devil took Jesus to a very high mountain and showed him all the world’s kingdoms and their splendor.
“I’ll give you all of this,” he said, “if you bow down and worship me.”
Jesus said, “Get away from me, Satan! Scripture says, ‘Worship the Lord your God, and serve only him.’”
Then the devil left, and angels came and cared for Jesus.
When Jesus heard that John had been arrested, he went back to Galilee.
He left Nazareth and settled in Capernaum by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali.
This fulfilled what God had spoken through Isaiah the prophet:
“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, beside the sea and beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations:
The people living in darkness have seen a great light; light has dawned on those living in the land and shadow of death.”
From then on, Jesus began preaching: “Turn back to God, because the Kingdom of Heaven is near!”
As Jesus walked beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon (also called Peter) and his brother Andrew, casting a net into the sea. They were fishermen.
“Come, follow me,” Jesus said, “and I’ll teach you to fish for people.”
Right away, they left their nets and followed him.
Going on from there, Jesus saw two more brothers: James, Zebedee’s son, and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, repairing their nets. Jesus called them.
They immediately left the boat and their father and followed him.
Jesus traveled throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, announcing the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every kind of disease and sickness among the people.

News about him spread through all Syria. People brought him everyone who was sick or suffering from various diseases and pain, people possessed by demons, those with seizures, and paralyzed people. Jesus healed them.
Large crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and the lands beyond the Jordan.
